publication: June 2025 tax ready reckoner: direct effects of illustrative tax changes (July 2026 update deferred by HMRC)
external_baseline: HMRC indexed baseline as of Spring Statement 2025; illustrative changes take effect April 2026
calendar_year_proxy: PolicyEngine calendar year Y proxies HMRC FY Y-(Y+1).
join_rule: external rows join on (program, subgroup == hmrc_label verbatim); measure_key is reckoner_202506__<program>__slug(label) — the program prefix is mandatory because HMRC prints identical labels under different tax heads (VAT and IPT both print 'Change standard rate by 1 percentage point')
parameter_path_verification: policyengine-uk was not installed at authoring. paths_verified: true means every path in the measure was resolved by data/uk/obr_measure_reforms.yaml (obr-costings-mode2) against pe-uk 2.89.2; false means candidate paths (or null) that the pipeline's --dry-run must resolve on the managed environment before any sim. A measure whose paths fail to resolve is demoted to pe_gap, never computed against a guessed parameter.

computability_triage.note: carrying_a_delta is the number the RUNTIME will compute. It must equal `expressible`: a partial measure with a delta computed a different reform from the one its label states, and made the runtime produce 27 ok / 48 gap against a declared 24 / 51.

head_variable_rule: Every measure carrying a delta names the PE head variable its revenue effect is read off, in the registry rather than in a dict inside the runtime. Employer NICs read `ni_employer`, not `national_insurance` — the committed campaign artifacts establish that head, and summing the employer measures through national_insurance reported an employee-side aggregate under an employer label.
gap_citation_rule: Every not_expressible measure carries an action_link, so its pe_gap row is a finding with somewhere to go rather than a blank (descriptive gate #9). The free-text `note` travels onto the staged row as an annotation and is never dropped at staging.

engine_pin.note: The version this registry's parameter paths were authored and verified against, and the version the merged campaign artifacts were computed at. The runtime REFUSES to compute against a different one: the earlier dry-run passed under whatever ambient policyengine-uk happened to be installed (2.75.3) while the registry prose referenced 2.89.2, so path resolution proved nothing about the engine the run would actually use.

baseline_honesty_rule: The run executes CURRENT LAW while the claim keys HMRC's indexed baseline (hmrc_indexed_baseline_spring_2025). Both keys are stamped — on the staged row and on the per-measure artifact — so the guard can VERIFY the two worlds differ instead of assuming, and every successful row is status `constructed`, never `ok` (which is not a valid ComparisonStatus at all). The merged campaign rows model this exactly.
